'''Pauline May Harrison''' (née '''Cowan''', 24 August 1926 – 28 May 2024) was a British protein [[crystallography|crystallographer]] and professor emeritus at the [[University of Sheffield]]. She gained her chemistry degree from [[Somerville College, Oxford]] in 1948, followed by a DPhil in X-ray crystallography in 1952 supervised by [[Dorothy Hodgkin]]. After three years at [[King's College London]] (contemporary with [[Rosalind Franklin]]) she moved to the [[University of Sheffield]] in 1955 as a demonstrator in the Biochemistry department (now Molecular Biology and Biotechnology), obtaining an [[Medical Research Council (United Kingdom)|MRC]] grant to study the iron storage protein [[Ferritin]], publishing preliminary X-ray diffraction data in the 1st volume of the [[Journal of Molecular Biology]] in 1959.<ref>{{citation |doi=10.1016/S0022-2836(59)80009-7 |title=The structures of ferritin and apoferritin: Some preliminary X-ray data|year=1959|last1=Harrison|first1=Pauline M.|journal=Journal of Molecular Biology|volume=1|pages=69–IN12}}</ref> The molecule which became her life's work.<ref>{{citation |url=https://www.sheffield.ac.uk/staff/portraits/paulineharrison |title= Pauline Harrison}}</ref><ref>{{citation |url= https://www.sheffield.ac.uk/mbb/welcome/namedchairs/pauline-harrison |title= Professor Pauline Harrison}}</ref> In 1978, she was awarded a [[personal chair]] and retired in 1991. In 2001 she was appointed a [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire|CBE]] for services to higher education.

==Personal life and death==
Harrison was the daughter of botanists [[Adeline May Cowan|Adeline May Organe]] and [[John Macqueen Cowan]], Assistant Keeper of the [[Royal Botanic Garden, Edinburgh]]. She was married to [[Royden Harrison]], also a lecturer at Sheffield and a figure in the Labour movement until his death in 2002. Harrison was an alumna of [[St. Trinnean's School]].<ref name=IWWW>{{citation |title=The International Who's Who of Women 2002 |editor=Elizabeth Sleeman |publisher=Psychology Press |year=2001 |isbn=9781857431223 |page=235}}</ref>

Harrison died on 28 May 2024, at the age of 97.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Funeral notice for Mrs Pauline May Harrison |url=https://www.dignityfunerals.co.uk/funeral-notices/28-05-2024-pauline-may-harrison/ |website=www.dignityfunerals.co.uk |language=en}}</ref>
